messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — I'm starting a small project to retire two legacy trace fields we put into events for cost attribution: `billing_key_v1` and `tenant_hint`. These are causing a bunch of edgecases in enrichment and downstream joins. Proposal below, looking for feedback + owners.

maya: +1, high time. can you paste the exact shape of old vs new so infra knows what to accept?

alex: Sure. Current: we have freeform `billing_key_v1` at the root and a `tenant_hint` tag in span attributes. Target: a normalized `billing.owner.id` and `billing.owner.type` inside the envelope meta. Plan: compatibility shim at ingestion for 6 weeks, then migrate transforms, then cut.

alex: Snippet of the mapping I'm proposing:
```
// incoming event root (old)
{
  "billing_key_v1": "acct-123:team-foo",
  "span": { "attributes": { "tenant_hint": "foo-team" } }
}

// normalized envelope (new)
{
  "meta": {
    "billing.owner.id": "acct-123/team-foo",
    "billing.owner.type": "team"
  }
}
```

devon: How does this affect sampling and our cost buckets? If we change keys we might spike cardinality during the migration.

alex: Good point. Migration strategy: 1) shim writes both old and new fields for events during the co-existence window, 2) we route the normalized field to the cost-aggregation join path (so downstream jobs only read normalized), 3) add a small sampler filter to detect rare owners and fold them into an "other" bucket for 30 days to keep cardinality bounded.

maya: For step 1, will shim live in the edge gateway or in the ingest lambda? I'd prefer gateway so we avoid churn in backfills.

alex: Gateway preferred. Lightweight transform: read old keys, emit `meta.billing.owner.*`. No writes to DB yet. We'll tag shimged events with `_meta_migrated=true` so we can query them.

infra-bot: deploy.gateway: canary deploy scheduled for 03/21 02:00 UTC -> will monitor error-rate and throughput.

devon: Backfills: we'll need a plan to backfill historic traces used for billing reconciliation. Are we ok with a one-time backfill job that populates normalized fields in the cold store?

alex: Yes — backfill in cold store only. Hot path will read normalized field from shim for new events. Backfill steps: create mapping job that reads old fields, writes normalized meta into backfill index. Run with rate-limit and sampling to avoid cluster pressure.

sara: Who owns the schema change in the obs gateway? Also, will alerting change? Our billing dashboards rely on `billing_key_v1` today.

alex: Ownership: infra-gateway team implements shim + tests; eng-platform owns the normalization spec and rollout playbook; biz-ops (cc @sara) owns dashboard migration. We'll create a dashboard sync runbook and update alerts to point at `meta.billing.owner.id` once backfill completes.

maya: One operational risk: some services already embed billing info inside payloads at higher cardinality (per-user). We should add a lint step in ingestion that rejects owner ids with `/user-` prefix or maps them to a `user-scoped` type.

alex: Agreed. Add policy: if owner id looks like a user, map type->`user-scoped` and collapse id to org-level unless flagged by a whitelist. We'll publish the whitelist to the oncall docs.

devon: Tests? We need unit tests for mapping, integration tests for gateway, and a small canary that verifies cost-aggregation results between old vs new keys for a 24h window.

alex: Plan to add: schema unit tests, integration test job that compares results on test cluster, and a 24h parallel run that writes to a shadow cost-agg topic. If parity is >= 99.5% for high-volume owners we proceed.

sara: Timeline and communication? finance needs at least 3 weeks notice before we alter billing pipelines.

alex: Timeline draft:
- Week 0: finalize mapping + policy, owner signoffs (this week)
- Week 1: gateway shim implementation + unit tests
- Week 2: canary deploy shim, run parallel cost-agg shadow for 7 days
- Week 3: run backfill staging, dashboard migration dry-run
- Week 4: cutover (disable legacy reads in transforms) and start final backfill
I'll sync with finance for the 3-week notice.

maya: Can I volunteer infra to implement the gateway part? devon can own the shadow cost-agg job.

devon: Yep, I'll make the shadow job and parity checks.

sara: I'll coordinate with finance and reps, and update the alert runbook.

alex: Awesome. Action items: alex->write spec doc and whitelist (by EOD), maya->implement shim (PR by end of week), devon->shadow job (P0 next week), sara->stakeholder comms. I'll open an RFC follow-up PR and link the playbook.

infra-bot: deploy.gateway: canary succeeded (2/2 hosts).

maya: started a draft PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingest/gateway/merge/1234 — still WIP but tests pass locally.

alex: Great — drop the PR link here when ready for review. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
